title: Share out the work
description:
Before starting worker threads, a program splits `total` items into `parts` contiguous ranges, one per thread. Write `splitRanges(total, parts)`, which returns `parts` pairs `{ begin, end }` (end is one past the last item) that together cover `0` to `total` exactly once, in order.

The ranges must be as even as possible: their sizes differ by at most one, with the **larger** ranges first.

```
splitRanges(10, 3)  ->  {0,4} {4,7} {7,10}     sizes 4, 3, 3
splitRanges(2, 4)   ->  {0,1} {1,2} {2,2} {2,2}
```

If `parts` is 0, return an empty vector.
hints: `total / parts` is the size every range gets at least; `total % parts` is how many items are left over.
Give one leftover item to each of the first `total % parts` ranges, and keep a running start position.
